To be clear, I am mostly talking about modding like in Call of Duty games.

So, I've been thinking about it for the last minute or so, and wanted to hear what your opinions are on the matter.

My 2 cents: I think modding is perfectly fine, if it's done correctly. What I mean by that is, mods should not be used to cheat the game or players, it should be used to add more playing value to a game/make it fun.

Like in Call of Duty 4, the game is pretty old now, and I hate to say it, pretty boring (don't get me wrong, I still love the game, but newer CoDs have spoiled me.). In CoD4's case, mods can give some extra life to it. For example, you can play game modes that are not present in the base game, like Zombieland (this mod is awesome - check some YouTube videos about it). Even other mods like high jump and unlimited ammo makes playing the game a blast.

I remember a while back where I was in a game where there were high jumping and unlimited ammo. This was one of the funnest moments in CoD4 for me. The way the characters fell when you killed them in mid air was pretty hilarious.

Unfortunately, this isn't where modding ends. There are times when modders think they're doing players "good" by giving them max rank and unlocking everything, which actually spoils the game for them IMO. I was in one of those lobbies. The game barely started, and I received a message saying that I've been promoted to level 55(max level), and that everything has been unlocked. It pissed me off, as I was looking forward to ranking up and unlocking shit for myself.

If you're going to give players max level and unlock everything, you should ask them if they want it. I know that there are actually players that would appreciate max rank and unlock all because they were deranked by a hacker.

Mods that I think should not be used at all:
- Invisibility
- Aimbot. Fuck aimbot. (Auto aim - every shot is a headshot, no matter where the enemy player is)
- Wallhack. (Can see and shoot through walls)
- Invincibility (God mode)
- Anti quit (Can't leave the match).

The above mentioned mods are only fun for the host of the game. You're pretty much fucked if you're not host, especially when anti quit is enabled. This ruins the game for everyone.

Anyway, that's pretty much it. I think mods are okay, as long as you're using it to make it fun for everyone, not just yourself.

What's your opinion?

Edit: Would like to say that your response does not have to be related to Call of Duty specifically, I used it because it's the only games I am familiar with that has online mods.
Game modding - what are your thoughts about it?

I play a lot of EU4 and Mount & Blade. These games simply wouldn't be as good as they are if mods weren't an option. This is doubly true for Mount & Blade, which has grown to the point of being virtually unplayable in its vanilla state, to me.

Of course, being an exclusively single-player gamer, I don't have a baseline similar to yours when it comes to cheating. Unless a modder throws in some unexpected easter eggs to a game I dislike, it's simply impossible for another person to "ruin" my gaming experience with mods.
Call of Duty logic at its finest.
